105.titulo: Participatory process for the development of Chile's Decentralization Policy
105.resumen: Implementation of a participatory process in all regions of the country for the construction of a decentralization policy for Chile
105.buenaPractica: Broad participatory process involving diverse actors, deployed across the country's 16 regions with the aim of facilitating citizen spaces for debate on the territory's vision of the future and the identification of key decentralization measures, within a planning horizon that transcends successive government administrations and serves as a guide for State action over the next ten years.
105.actores: UNDP (support), SUBDERE, community actors, civil society, productive sectors, and others from all regions of the country.
105.institucion: Subsecretaría de Desarrollo Regional y Administrativo (SUBDERE) (Chile)

106.titulo: Generation of inputs for the development of the Valparaíso Regional Development Strategy (ERD) 2025 - 2035
106.resumen: Broad participatory process at the territorial level to develop the ERD.
106.buenaPractica: Participatory process across the entire region, including the island territories of Rapa Nui and Juan Fernández, in which foresight methodologies and the mapping of future scenarios were applied to design the Regional Development Strategy 2025-2035.
106.actores: UNDP (support throughout the process), Regional Government of Valparaíso, Regional Council, civil society organizations, and actors from all sectors across the different territories of the Valparaíso Region (participation of more than 1,600 people).

107.titulo: Plan Económico Sinaloa 2050: participatory construction of a long-term development vision
107.resumen: Process driven by CODESIN with technical support from UNDP to build a shared vision of Sinaloa's development toward 2050. The initiative combines analysis of global trends and megatrends, territorial diagnosis, capacity building in foresight, and multisectoral dialogue mechanisms to identify challenges, opportunities, and strategic priorities for the state's future.
107.buenaPractica: Incorporation of foresight and anticipatory governance tools into a long-term territorial planning exercise, bringing together actors from the public, private, academic, and social sectors around a shared vision of the future. The process seeks to strengthen institutional capacity to anticipate structural changes, reduce reactive decision-making, and promote more resilient and sustainable strategies.
107.actores: Consejo para el Desarrollo Económico de Sinaloa (CODESIN); Multisectoral Technical Team (ETM) of the Plan Sinaloa 2050, composed of representatives and local experts from academic institutions, the business sector, local governments, and civil society organizations participating in the consultation and dialogue processes.
107.institucion: Consejo para el Desarrollo Económico de Sinaloa (CODESIN)
107.comentarios: The experience represents a practical application of strategic foresight approaches at the subnational level. It stands out for combining evidence generation, capacity building, and participatory processes to incorporate a long-term perspective into the definition of territorial development priorities. Its methodology can serve as a reference for other states interested in integrating strategic anticipation into their planning processes.

108.resumen: The project seeks to strengthen the State's decentralization process through multilevel coordination instruments and strengthened capacities from a territorial approach. Within this framework, technical assistance has been provided to various processes, including the formulation of the National Multisectoral Decentralization Policy.
108.buenaPractica: Incorporation of a long-term strategic vision, projected to 2040, to guide territorial governance and the decentralization process. The experience promotes multilevel and multisectoral coordination as well as strategic planning with inputs from the planning of regional and local governments and sectors; territorial management and multilevel coordination. Around 40 participatory spaces for consultation and dialogue have been generated with national and subnational actors.
108.actores: UNDP, Decentralization Secretariat of the PCM, regional and local governments, territorial actors.

109.titulo: Social Management and Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue Project
109.resumen: Seeks to strengthen the State's capacities to prevent and manage social conflicts, as well as to support the design and implementation of the National Multisectoral Policy for the Prevention and Management of Social Conflicts.
109.buenaPractica: The experience links the participatory design of a national policy, through decentralized citizen consultations, with the territorial strengthening of capacities and instruments for the prevention of social conflicts, such as early warning systems and information management to improve conflict typologies and response protocols; and the reinforcement of dialogue and conflict prevention offices in regional governments.
109.actores: UNDP, Secretariat for Social Management and Dialogue of the PCM, regional governments

110.titulo: Project for the Promotion of Dialogue and Consolidation of the Acuerdo Nacional
110.resumen: Promotion of political dialogue and consensus building within the framework of the Acuerdo Nacional on priority issues for democratic governance and the country's development.
110.buenaPractica: The Acuerdo Nacional, as the national consensus-building platform, sustains spaces for dialogue, both formal and informal, in which strategic challenges of national interest are anticipated and addressed, promoting political agreements that seek to guide medium- and long-term responses.
110.actores: UNDP, National Secretariat of the Acuerdo Nacional (PCM), authorities and sectors, social organizations, political parties, among others

111.resumen: Application of strategic foresight methodologies to identify future scenarios for justice, emerging risks, and the institutional capacities needed for the transformation of the judicial system.
111.buenaPractica: Introduction of anticipatory governance and futures thinking into judicial planning.
111.actores: Judiciary, UNDP, and the participation of 2,082 key justice actors; 201 representatives from academia, civil society, and churches; 25 political aides; and 61 actors from the business sector.

112.titulo: Ten-Year Strategic Plan of the Judiciary
112.resumen: Institutional transformation roadmap focused on modernization, digitalization, access to justice, and strengthening citizen trust.
112.buenaPractica: Long-term planning with monitoring indicators and alignment with SDG 16.
112.actores: UNDP, AECID, World Justice Project and Together Ideas, drawing on a participatory process that involved more than 3,000 national actors
112.comentarios: Regional benchmark in strategic judicial planning

113.titulo: Creation of the Ministry of Justice
113.resumen: Technical assistance for the institutional design, competencies, and roadmap for the creation of a new Ministry of Justice.
113.buenaPractica: Institutional reorganization of the justice sector under a vision of integrated governance.
113.comentarios: One of the most significant institutional reforms of the justice sector in the Caribbean.

114.titulo: Strengthening social participation and citizen oversight of policies for persons with disabilities
114.resumen: Development and implementation of participatory methodologies to support the formulation and improvement of public policies aimed at persons with disabilities, including the V National Conference on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and civil society listening workshops on the biopsychosocial assessment of disability. The initiative encompassed methodological design, the mobilization of key actors, the facilitation of participatory processes, and the systematization of contributions to support decision-making processes and regulatory development.
114.buenaPractica: The experience combines different mechanisms of social participation —such as national conferences, thematic workshops, and processes for systematizing contributions— strengthening dialogue between government and civil society and expanding the incorporation of the demands of persons with disabilities into public policy formulation. This model generated relevant inputs for improving the biopsychosocial assessment of disability and for the institutional strengthening of the National Secretariat for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (SNDPD).
114.actores: SNDPD/MDHC, UNDP, FLACSO, CONADE, state and municipal councils, organizations of persons with disabilities, and civil society.
114.institucion: Ministério dos Direitos Humanos e da Cidadania
114.comentarios: The experience supported the reactivation of national mechanisms for social participation and expanded qualified listening to civil society in strategic processes for the implementation and guarantee of the rights of persons with disabilities.

115.resumen: As part of its strategy to strengthen democratic governance and promote consensus building around sustainable development challenges, Pontes para Convergências promoted the creation of a multi-stakeholder platform conceived as a permanent space for dialogue, coordination, and democratic innovation. The platform seeks to connect representatives of the public sector, civil society, academia, the private sector, the media, and youth organizations to foster knowledge exchange, the identification of shared priorities, and the formulation of collaborative solutions.
115.buenaPractica: As the governance mechanism for this initiative, a Strategic Council was established, composed of leaders from diverse sectors and backgrounds, ensuring plurality of perspectives, representativeness, and the legitimacy of decision-making processes. This model strengthens collaborative governance by promoting the participation of multiple actors in defining common agendas, while contributing to an anticipatory governance capable of identifying trends, risks, and opportunities for the future of democracy in Brazil
115.comentarios: Conceived as a permanent space for dialogue, exchange, and collective construction, the platform seeks to build consensus around complex challenges affecting contemporary democracies, promoting collaboration among public institutions, academia, civil society, the private sector, the media, and youth organizations.

116.resumen: The Pena Justa initiative is part of the Brazilian State's efforts to address structural rights violations in the prison system, recognized by the Supreme Federal Court in ADPF 347, which declared an "unconstitutional state of affairs." The project seeks to strengthen access to justice and promote more equitable decisions in criminal matters through inter-institutional coordination, evidence generation, and the development of tools that reduce inequalities and promote a rights-centered approach.
116.buenaPractica: Use of evidence and data to guide more equitable judicial decisions. Inter-institutional coordination among the justice system, international cooperation, and social actors. Focus on intersectionality (gender, race, vulnerability). Development of replicable methodologies for other contexts within the justice system
116.actores: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), National Council of Justice (CNJ), Supreme Federal Court (with regard to ADPF 347), justice system actors, and civil society
116.comentarios: The experience operationalizes, in the public policy sphere, the structural determinations derived from ADPF 347, contributing to the strengthening of the rule of law and the achievement of SDG 16. It has potential for replicability in other contexts of criminal justice system reform in Latin America.

117.titulo: National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights
117.resumen: Participatory construction of the first National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights, aligned with the UN Guiding Principles.
117.buenaPractica: Coordination among the public sector, private sector, civil society, and academia.
117.actores: Ministry of Labor, Ministry of Human Rights, UNDP
117.comentarios: Emblematic experience for integrating corporate sustainability, due diligence, and human rights.

118.titulo: National Action Coalition on Information Integrity and Elections
118.resumen: Governance Roundtable for Information Integrity in Electoral Processes, created and led by SERVEL and UNDP Chile, with the aim of promoting an information ecosystem with integrity in the lead-up to the country's elections.
118.buenaPractica: It constitutes a collaborative working space and partnership between public and private actors to confront information pollution and toxic communication in electoral contexts. Its main milestones include the signing of an ethical commitment to electoral information integrity in September 2025, and the launch of the campaign "Infórmate con Responsabilidad, Participa con Integridad" (Get Informed Responsibly, Participate with Integrity).
118.actores: The Roundtable is led by UNDP and SERVEL, and brings together representatives of digital platforms, traditional media, civil society organizations, and academia.
118.comentarios: In parallel, UNDP implemented the eMonitor+ tool for monitoring social media around information pollution and provided inputs for the Roundtable's action. Platforms such as Meta, TikTok, Google, and X implemented specific civic products for the electoral process, while organizations such as Malaespina and Fundación Ciudadanía Inteligente developed verification and citizen guidance tools, consolidating the Roundtable as a pioneering model of multisectoral collaboration for information integrity in electoral contexts

119.titulo: Strengthening governance and the participation of children and adolescents in the territory
119.resumen: Establishment of a Regional Advisory Council for Children and Adolescents and of the Leadership and Union Network for Children and Adolescents (Red LUNA), composed of children and adolescents.
119.buenaPractica: The Advisory Council for Children and Adolescents and Red LUNA operated as permanent and complementary mechanisms —adults and children/adolescents— which, with technical support from UNDP and the Regional Government (GORE) and the coordination of various regional institutions linked to childhood and adolescence, participatorily co-constructed the Regional Action Plan for Children and Adolescents, integrating territorial, intercultural, and rights-based approaches.
119.actores: UNDP, Regional Government of Los Ríos, various relevant regional actors in matters of childhood and adolescence; representative of children and adolescents
119.comentarios: Pioneering model of regional governance on childhood and adolescence in Chile.

120.titulo: Governance and planning for disaster risk reduction in the Valparaíso region
120.resumen: Pilot of collaborative work among the regional, municipal, and sectoral levels to strengthen planning and coordination in the face of disasters.
120.buenaPractica: A collaboration mechanism was created in which UNDP acts as a methodological bridge to integrate SENAPRED's official standards, the territorial knowledge of the municipalities, and the regional government's planning frameworks to produce communal plans that are technically sound and territorially relevant.
120.actores: UNDP (support), Regional Government of Valparaíso, National Disaster Prevention and Response Service (SENAPRED), Association of Municipalities of the Valparaíso Region
120.comentarios: The success of the pilot has made it possible to move forward with a new project to support more municipalities and lay the foundations for a regional governance framework for DRR with community involvement.

121.titulo: Implementation of the Agrarian and Rural Jurisdiction
121.resumen: Support for the launch of the new agrarian jurisdiction created to resolve conflicts related to land access and use.
121.buenaPractica: Territorial access-to-justice approach and strengthening of rural judicial capacities.
121.actores: UNDP, FAO, Ministry of Justice and Law, in the PDET municipalities of San Juan Nepomuceno, Zambrano, and El Carmen de Bolívar.
121.comentarios: A strategic experience for the implementation of the Peace Agreement and the reduction of territorial inequalities.

122.resumen: Pioneering instrument that incorporates a human and comprehensive security approach, articulating citizen security, democratic governance, human rights, prevention, and risk management.
122.buenaPractica: Moving beyond exclusively police-centered approaches through a comprehensive, people-centered vision.
122.actores: Coordinating Ministry of Security, UNDP, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility, Ministry of the Interior, Ministry of National Defense, National Risk and Emergency Management Service; Strategic Intelligence Center

123.titulo: "Tejiendo Ciudadanía: Encuentros por el Perú" (Weaving Citizenship: Gatherings for Peru)
123.resumen: The Tejiendo Ciudadanía initiative organized 4 macro-regional gatherings to address, in a participatory and decentralized manner, the country's governance and sustainable development challenges, with the participation of 310 organizations from civil society, the public and private sectors, academia, and the media.
123.buenaPractica: Building a network of allies that made it possible to reach and include underrepresented actors in public debate, such as universities and the media, in a decentralized manner. As a result, a Citizen Agenda with proposals was developed, capturing concerns shared across the country as well as those specific to each macro-region.
123.actores: UNDP, Grupo La República, Instituto de Estudios Peruanos, Red Científica Peruana, 17 universities in various regions, and regional media outlets.
123.institucion: UNDP Peru, media organizations, think tanks, and universities. Close coordination and delivery of the Citizen Agenda to the Acuerdo Nacional (Presidency of the Council of Ministers)

124.titulo: Decentralization of the National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights
124.resumen: Territorial adaptation and implementation of the National Plan on Business and Human Rights through regional governments and local actors.
124.buenaPractica: Territorialization of the BHR agenda and strengthening of local capacities.
124.actores: UNDP, National Government of Peru, Japanese companies, their suppliers and partners
124.institucion: Ministry of Justice and Human Rights
124.comentarios: Considered one of the most advanced experiences in localizing the Business and Human Rights agenda.

125.titulo: Independent Technical Study (ETI) of Block 8, an experience of intercultural dialogue and participation
125.resumen: Participatory and intercultural development of the ETI for Block 8, combining technical assessment with dialogue management, mediation, and coordination between the State and Indigenous federations for environmental remediation, in an area of high conflict and oil activity in the Peruvian Amazon.
125.buenaPractica: Participatory and intercultural governance model based on a tripartite Monitoring Committee (State-federations-UNDP) as a space for dialogue, coordination, and consensus-based decision-making, with transparency, follow-up on agreements, and legitimacy.

126.resumen: Process of building a comprehensive public security policy based on evidence, citizen participation, and inter-institutional coordination to address homicides, gender-based violence, firearms, drug trafficking, cybercrime, and violence prevention.
126.buenaPractica: Incorporation of citizen participation mechanisms and an open government approach in the formulation of the security policy.

127.titulo: National Program to Confront Political Gender-Based Violence in the 2024 Elections
127.resumen: The initiative, developed by the Federal Public Defender's Office (DPU) in collaboration with UNDP, aims to prevent, raise the visibility of, and confront political gender-based violence during the 2024 electoral process in Brazil. The program articulates communication strategies, reporting channels, and free legal assistance, helping to guarantee the exercise of women's political rights and to strengthen democracy. The initiative incorporates the production of information, awareness-raising campaigns, and victim support mechanisms, promoting a safer and more inclusive communication ecosystem.
127.buenaPractica: Creation of accessible and safe channels for reporting and assisting victims. Strategic use of public communication to raise the visibility of political gender-based violence. Generation and systematization of data on cases and profiles of violence. Inter-institutional coordination (justice system, electoral system, and international organizations). Integration of legal assistance with communication strategies and rights education [direitoshu...dpu.def.br]
127.actores: Federal Public Defender's Office (DPU), United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), Electoral Justice (TSE and TREs), Ministry of Women and other public institutions, civil society and support networks for women in politics
127.comentarios: The experience strengthens communication governance by integrating information, legal assistance, and social awareness-raising to confront political gender-based violence, recognized in Brazil as a crime aimed at restricting women's political participation. It also contributes to SDGs 5 (gender equality), 10 (reduced inequalities), and 16 (strong institutions), with high potential for replication in Latin America.

128.titulo: "Infórmate con Responsabilidad, Participa con Integridad" Campaign (Get Informed Responsibly, Participate with Integrity)
128.resumen: Communication campaign aimed at strengthening citizen trust and the quality of public debate, fostering informed participation and the responsible exercise of the right to vote.
128.buenaPractica: The campaign invited citizens to get informed responsibly and participate with integrity in the 2025 electoral process, promoting a plural, transparent, and respectful communication environment.

129.resumen: Creation of the Ama Llulla network to strengthen access to verified information and citizen trust in the face of disinformation in electoral contexts.
129.buenaPractica: The first collaborative media network and platform against disinformation in Peru, bringing together more than 20 local and digital media outlets for fact-checking using technological tools and artificial intelligence (AI), including translation into Indigenous languages.

130.titulo: Bringing the State Closer to Citizens Project
130.resumen: Contributes to improving citizens' access to public government information by strengthening strategic public communication and the State's communication management.
130.buenaPractica: Decentralized capacity building for communication teams, generation of evidence for decision-making, and coordination across sectors. Communication preparedness for crisis and emergency situations.
130.actores: UNDP, Secretariat of Social Communication (PCM), communication teams of subnational governments and sectors
130.institucion: Presidency of the Council of Ministers (PCM)

131.resumen: Implementation of an AI-based tool to characterize the presence and dynamics of electoral information pollution in the Peruvian digital ecosystem, as well as to analyze the incidence of toxic communication, hate speech, and gender-based violence in digital communications linked to electoral processes.
131.buenaPractica: Combines technological innovation with citizen participation and knowledge generation. Universities have been involved, particularly faculty and students, in using the tool for digital information monitoring and analysis. It seeks to facilitate early warning mechanisms and provide useful information for preventing risks that may affect the integrity of electoral processes.

132.resumen: Working group composed of public, private, civil society, and academic institutions to promote integrity and anti-corruption in Chile, with a view to implementing the United Nations Convention against Corruption in the country.
132.buenaPractica: The Alliance, led by UNDP and the Office of the Comptroller General of the Republic, has enabled the coordination of different sectors and entities around integrity, something not otherwise contemplated in the institutional design; it leverages synergies and avoids fragmentation and duplication in promotion, training, and dissemination activities, as well as in highlighting good practices and conducting legislative monitoring. Within the framework of the Alliance, support is coordinated for municipalities across the country in developing and adopting codes of ethics.
132.actores: The Alliance was founded by UNDP and the Office of the Comptroller General of the Republic, which hold its Executive Coordination. It comprises 45 entities, including the main public institutions concerned with integrity and anti-corruption, trade associations, universities, and civil society organizations.

133.resumen: Creation of an innovation laboratory to promote evidence in the face of corruption and public integrity challenges.
133.buenaPractica: An open platform for experimentation, co-creation, dialogue, and dissemination that seeks to bring together the State, civil society, academia, the private sector, and international cooperation to generate evidence, applied research, and innovative solutions on transparency and integrity, with a focus on improving public policies and services.
133.actores: UNDP, Proética (Peruvian Chapter of Transparency International), regional/local actors
133.institucion: UNDP Peru, Proética (Peruvian Chapter of Transparency International)

134.resumen: Development of indicators on judicial performance, accessibility, and open justice to monitor institutional results.
134.buenaPractica: Use of evidence for decision-making and continuous improvement of judicial services.
134.comentarios: Linked to Open Justice initiatives and the Justice Action Coalition.

135.titulo: National Diagnostic on Online Sexual Violence against Children and Adolescents and contributions to the Digital ECA
135.resumen: Applied research initiative aimed at identifying and analyzing risks, actors, services, regulatory frameworks, and good practices related to online sexual violence against children and adolescents. The work produced evidence and recommendations oriented toward strengthening public policies for the protection of rights in digital environments.
135.buenaPractica: The experience is an example of evidence-based digital governance, bringing together academia, government, the rights guarantee system, the private sector, and civil society to support the formulation of public policies and regulatory frameworks aimed at the comprehensive protection of children and adolescents in the digital environment
135.actores: MDHC, UNDP, UFRN/OBIJUV, CONANDA, Sistema de Garantia de Direitos, technology companies, civil society organizations, and specialists
135.institucion: Ministério dos Direitos Humanos e da Cidadania
135.comentarios: The experience contributed to generating knowledge and recommendations that served as a basis for national debates on the protection of children and adolescents in the digital environment, as well as for initiatives linked to the Digital ECA.

136.resumen: The Unified Electronic Enforcement System (SEEU) is a digital platform that centralizes and automates the management of criminal enforcement proceedings in Brazil. Developed by the National Council of Justice (CNJ) within the framework of the Fazendo Justiça Program, the system enables the national integration of prison and judicial data, contributing to more accurate oversight of sentence compliance and to guaranteeing the rights of persons deprived of liberty. The SEEU promotes greater transparency, efficiency, and legal certainty in criminal enforcement.
136.buenaPractica: Comprehensive digitalization of criminal enforcement proceedings National integration of judicial and prison information Reduction of errors in the calculation of sentences and time served Improved transparency and access to information Strengthening of data-driven decision-making in the justice system
136.actores: National Council of Justice (CNJ) Fazendo Justiça Program (CNJ/UNDP) United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) State Courts of Justice Brazilian prison system
136.comentarios: The SEEU is considered one of the main digital transformation tools of the Brazilian justice system, contributing directly to overcoming structural problems identified in criminal enforcement, including those highlighted in ADPF 347. The experience has high replicability potential in other countries of the region as a model of digital governance applied to justice.

137.resumen: Digital platform for monitoring, visualizing, and analyzing information on human rights and groups in situations of vulnerability.
137.buenaPractica: Use of open data and analytics to strengthen accountability and public policies.
137.actores: UNDP, Ombudsperson's Office (Defensoría de los Habitantes), National Human Rights Observatory (ONADH)
137.comentarios: Regional benchmark for national human rights institutions.

138.titulo: SISJUPAZ - Single Justice of the Peace System
138.resumen: Digital system to strengthen the management and coordination of justice of the peace in Peru.
138.buenaPractica: First digital system exclusively for justices of the peace in the country, designed through a co-diagnostic process and adaptation to territorial needs, which facilitates case registration and follow-up, coordination with the ordinary justice system, and the generation of evidence for decision-making. Piloted in 4 judicial districts of the country, with technological equipment and training for its use.

139.titulo: Single Digital Platform for the Prevention and Management of Social Conflicts of the Peruvian State
139.resumen: Strengthening of a single, interoperable digital platform for the management of social conflicts.
139.buenaPractica: Coordinates information between the Executive Branch and subnational governments, strengthens early warning systems, and improves the follow-up of commitments for more timely, evidence-based decision-making.
139.institucion: Presidency of the Council of Ministers (PCM)

140.titulo: AILA: Artificial Intelligence Landscape Assessment – Peru
140.resumen: Readiness assessment for the responsible adoption of AI (ecosystem, AI for government, and regulation/ethics), with recommendations and a roadmap.
140.buenaPractica: Collaborative development of a comprehensive national diagnostic on the responsible use of AI, through consultations with experts and multisectoral actors, to strengthen institutional capacities and support the development of the National AI Strategy.
140.institucion: Presidency of the Council of Ministers (PCM)

141.resumen: Technical support for the evolution of the Sayhuite tool into GeoPerú, assisting the PCM in the technological migration process, coordination between secretariats, and the strengthening of regional and local government capacities for the use of geospatial information.
141.buenaPractica: Strengthens data governance through the integration and interoperability of territorial information from different public entities. Promotes evidence-based management for territorial planning and public decision-making.
141.actores: UNDP, PCM (Secretariats of Decentralization, and of Government and Digital Transformation)
141.institucion: Presidency of the Council of Ministers (PCM)

142.resumen: Early warning system that enables the identification, monitoring, and reporting of incidents and potential electoral conflicts, facilitating timely responses by electoral bodies.
142.buenaPractica: Its implementation was based on a participatory approach and institutional ownership from the initial design stages. The experience involved broad consultations with state and civil society actors, capacity building, protocol development, and technological adaptation to national needs. Promotion of institutional sustainability, inter-institutional coordination, and preventive capacities for the early management of electoral risks.

143.resumen: Technical assistance for the design and development of the first phases of the observatory, intended to integrate, systematize, and analyze information on social conflict through digital tools and early warning mechanisms.
143.buenaPractica: Incorporates tools for real-time analysis of information from diverse sources, data visualization, and georeferenced monitoring, facilitating informed decision-making and the timely identification of emerging trends and risks. Seeks to promote a more strategic and preventive management of social conflict.

144.titulo: JUSTINA – Intelligent Assistant for Justice and Security
144.resumen: Artificial intelligence tool integrated into the UNDP Solutions Radar to support policy design, comparative analysis, identification of good practices, and programmatic formulation.
144.buenaPractica: Application of AI as a digital public good to strengthen institutional capacities and accelerate knowledge transfer.

145.titulo: PRONASCI Youth – Tô de Boa: pathways toward a drug policy with racial justice for youth
145.resumen: Comprehensive prevention strategy aimed at adolescents and young people from territories in situations of vulnerability, developed by the National Secretariat for Drug Policies and Asset Management (SENAD) in partnership with UNDP. The initiative combines productive inclusion, income generation, community strengthening, biopsychosocial development, and the promotion of life projects, linking citizen security, social assistance, education, and community participation policies. The experience was subsequently incorporated as a reference for the implementation of the PRONASCI Youth program.
145.buenaPractica: The experience adopts a territorial and intergenerational approach to preventing violence associated with illicit drug markets, placing young people as protagonists of social transformation and promoting coordination among families, schools, public services, and community leaders. The model integrates principles of racial justice, human development, and the use of evidence for the continuous improvement of public policies.
145.actores: SENAD/MJSP, UNDP, Fiocruz, local governments, civil society organizations, community leaders, families, and participating youth
145.institucion: Ministério da Justiça e da Segurança Pública
145.comentarios: The evaluation of the experience contributed to improving public policies on drugs and violence prevention aimed at youth. The launch of the publication "Tô de Boa – Pathways toward a drug policy with racial justice for youth" took place jointly with the installation of the PRONASCI Youth Management Committee – Rio de Janeiro, demonstrating the incorporation of the project's lessons and results into the expansion and strengthening of this public policy.

146.resumen: The Dialogues with Youth project is part of the Justiça Plural Program, an initiative of the National Council of Justice (CNJ) in cooperation with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). Its objective is to promote engagement and dialogue between actors of the Judiciary and young people around debates on human rights and access to justice. The main planned activity is the holding of workshops in public secondary schools, facilitated by judges. These activities will address topics such as ethnic-racial equity, digital citizenship, and climate justice, always linked to guaranteeing access to justice.
146.buenaPractica: One of the main good practices of the Dialogues with Youth project is its ability to bring the Judiciary closer to young people through spaces for direct dialogue in public schools, promoting a closer, more accessible, and trust-based relationship. Through a participatory methodology adapted to youth language, the project encourages reflection on human rights, digital citizenship, ethnic-racial equity, and climate justice, connecting these topics with access to justice. It also highlights the coordination among public institutions, international organizations, and civil society, combining technical, pedagogical, and institutional expertise to strengthen civic education and youth participation.
146.actores: UNDP Brazil; Conselho Nacional de Justiça - CNJ;
146.comentarios: The systematization of the pilot experience is also a good practice, as it generates evidence and lessons learned to replicate and scale up the initiative in other territories of the country.

147.resumen: The initiative implemented various actions aimed at strengthening civic space, youth participation, and intergenerational governance. These include: (i) the launch of the regional survey "Bridges for Convergence – Voices of Youth," aimed at young people aged 18 to 29 in Latin America and the Caribbean; (ii) the organization of the multi-stakeholder gathering "Governments of the Future: Youth Expectations for Democracy"; and (iii) regional coordination with the Regional Bureau for Latin America and the Caribbean (RBLAC) for the implementation of the Policy Labs on Youth and Democracy. These actions promoted inclusive participation, democratic dialogue, and the incorporation of evidence and youth perspectives into debates on public policies and democratic governance.
147.buenaPractica: The Bridges for Convergence project promoted the effective participation of youth in spaces for dialogue and public policy-making, moving from a consultation approach to a model of co-creation and advocacy. The combination of participatory methodologies, intergenerational dialogue, and advocacy mechanisms strengthened trust between generations, broadened the representation of diverse voices, and generated strategic inputs for more inclusive, collaborative, and future-oriented governance.
147.comentarios: Through innovative mechanisms such as the regional survey Voices of Youth, the Policy Labs, the Fishbowl methodology, and digital tools, young people were able to interact directly with authorities, specialists, and decision-makers, contributing concrete proposals on the region's democratic challenges. This process culminated in the drafting of the Youth Charter for the Future of Democracy – Brasilia Declaration, a collectively built document that gathers priorities and recommendations to strengthen democracy, inclusion, and citizen participation.

148.resumen: Network and digital platform to enhance citizen participation and public advocacy by youth.
148.buenaPractica: Co-creation of proposed solutions to the country's challenges by youth, compiled in the digital public agenda "Portafolio Redpública," through digital tools and participatory spaces such as citizen consultations, festivals, hackathons, youth volunteering, chatbots, and decentralized information modules in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. Channeling of digital consultations on topics of youth interest in support of processes led by the National Youth Secretariat.

149.resumen: Participatory process carried out in 12 regions of the country to channel youth advocacy through the identification of territorial problems and the formulation of proposed solutions by young people, within the framework of "Tejiendo Ciudadanía: Encuentros por el Perú."
149.buenaPractica: Meaningful decentralized youth participation through a methodology that ensured territorial representation and the collective construction of proposals. The experience strengthened youth leadership and the incorporation of their perspectives into a process of macro-regional dialogues resulting in a citizen agenda. Partnerships with universities to expand reach.
